sources.title: Faster sorting algorithms discovered using deep reinforcement learning
sources.authors_note: Daniel J. Mankowitz, Andrea Michi, Anton Zhernov, et al.; complete author list retained at source
evidence_supported: AlphaDev used deep reinforcement learning to search for improved sorting routines.
The paper reports fixed sort 3, sort 4 and sort 5 algorithms and variable-sort results.
The fixed sort 3, sort 4 and sort 5 algorithms were reverse engineered into C++ and integrated into LLVM libc++.
The paper reports improvements up to 70% for short sequences and about 1.7% for sequences exceeding 250,000 elements in the described libc++ integration context.
Nature manuscript received, accepted, and publication dates are publication-process dates and do not by themselves establish the internal algorithm discovery date.

sources.title: AlphaDev discovers faster sorting algorithms
evidence_supported: DeepMind publicly announced AlphaDev on the Nature publication date.
The announcement describes reinforcement-learning-discovered sorting algorithms translated to C++ and available in LLVM libc++.
It reports improvements up to 70% for shorter sequences and about 1.7% for sequences exceeding 250,000 elements.

sources.title: D118029 Introduce branchless sorting functions for sort3, sort4 and sort5
sources.author: Marco Gelmi
evidence_supported: The review explicitly says the branchless sort3, sort4 and sort5 functions were generated using reinforcement learning.
The patch targeted integral types and included libc++ benchmarks on Skylake, ARM and AMD architectures.
The public review existed months before the Nature manuscript received date.
The revision was accepted after review and closed by the LLVM commit.
The commit installs branchless sort support used for small fixed-size sorting paths in libc++.
The source-level integration date is independently earlier than the Nature manuscript received date.

candidate_generation_date.rationale: The LLVM review for reinforcement-learning-generated sort routines was public by 2022-01-24 and landed in April 2022, so the later Nature manuscript received date cannot represent algorithm candidate generation. The exact internal discovery date remains unestablished.

evidenced_verification_events.event: LLVM review opened with benchmark and correctness-review surface
LLVM revision accepted and ready to land

verification_date.rationale: Correctness tests, hardware benchmarks, code review and journal review are distinct verification processes. The current evidence does not justify one canonical algorithm-verification date.

public_disclosure_date.rationale: LLVM review publicly exposed the reinforcement-learning-generated integration before the later formal research announcement.

acceptance_date.publication_process_note: Nature manuscript acceptance occurred 2023-03-23 but is not silently recoded as disciplinary acceptance.

technology_dependency.rationale: The target routines were generated through the AlphaDev reinforcement-learning search system, while the production integration also required human translation, code review, benchmarking and LLVM maintenance.

discrepancies.finding: The seed proxy postdates public LLVM review and integration evidence.
discrepancies.action: Do not silently recode; preserve for governed discrepancy adjudication.

discrepancies.finding: The seed proxy is the Nature manuscript acceptance date while software verification/review events occurred in 2022.
discrepancies.action: Do not silently recode; split verification events before any future ledger amendment.
